archetype.name: Underachiever (run-differential victim)
archetype.definition: A team whose run differential was eighth-best in the league and implied a division-winning record, but which finished ten games under .500 after losing more close games than anyone and having one catastrophic month.

report.headline: A playoff-caliber run differential buried under the league's worst close-game luck.

recap.finish: 76-86, fourth in the AL Central, nine games behind CLE; missed the postseason
recap.body:
On the margin, this was not a losing team. Detroit outscored opponents by 0.44 runs per game, eighth in the league and slightly better than the 87-win 2025 club's 0.41. It finished 76-86 anyway. Its W vs Run Diff of -12.6 was the worst in the league, which puts its run-differential record near 88-89 wins. That would have beaten Cleveland's 85-77 for the division. The Tigers had posted positive W vs Run Diff marks in 2021 through 2023, so a full season of close-game losses at this scale stands out.

The season went wrong in May. After a 14-13 April, Detroit went 6-22, scoring 81 runs and allowing 129. That one month accounts for most of the season's damage: outside May the team went 70-64 and outscored opponents by 119 runs. June and July looked like a contender, 30-20 with 263 runs scored and 174 allowed. August cooled to 11-16 despite a slightly positive run margin. September was 13-12. The closing ten games followed the season's pattern. Five of the six losses came by two runs, and both of the last two wins came by one.

Run prevention held the team up. The staff's 3.67 ERA ranked sixth and the defense ranked seventh in runs allowed, though the peripherals were less convincing. Troy Melton's 2.76 ERA sat well under his 4.09 FIP. Keider Montero (3.48 ERA, 1.04 WHIP) and Framber Valdez's 174 innings gave the rotation stability, which is why it graded only C+ despite the results. The bullpen graded C and was thinner than its ERAs suggest. Kyle Finnegan (5.42 FIP, 12.6% BB %) and Tyler Kinley (5.21 FIP) took heavy setup work with 28 holds between them. A relief corps walking that many hitters is a plausible contributor to the close-game record. The fielders also cost 21.1 runs, 24th in the league, a long way from the +12.4 of 2024.

The lineup was more top-heavy than its 11th-ranked .720 OPS suggests, which explains the D+ hitters grade. Kevin McGonigle (5.4 WAR, 129 wRC+, .376 OBP) and Dillon Dingler (5.0 WAR, 27 HR, +6.8 Def Runs behind the plate) were All-Star-level cornerstones. Riley Greene's 136 wRC+ was the best bat on the team. Below them, playing time went to weak hitters. Zach McKinstry took 423 PA at a 65 wRC+, and Matt Vierling's 61 wRC+ in 291 PA ended on the 60-day injured list. Spencer Torkelson hit 26 homers with a 115 wRC+, but his -7.2 Def Runs held his WAR to 1.2.

The end result is a third straight winning-caliber run differential that, for the first time in that run, did not produce a winning record. The 11-win drop from 2025 is mostly sequencing, not a collapse in talent.

highlights.title: Margin of a division winner
highlights.body: A +0.44 run differential per game ranked eighth in the league and edged the 2025 team's mark. The underlying team was at least as good as the two that reached October, which is the most important fact this season leaves behind.

highlights.title: McGonigle and Dingler as cornerstones
highlights.body: McGonigle's 5.4 WAR came with a .376 OBP from shortstop, and Dingler added 5.0 WAR with 27 homers and positive catcher defense. Both made the All-Star team and ranked fourth at their positions on the site. Two up-the-middle players this productive give the roster a solid core to build around.

highlights.title: Summer form of a contender
highlights.body: June and July went 30-20 with a +89 run margin, the team's real level when healthy and settled. Combined with a 13-12 September, it shows the May collapse was the outlier rather than the norm.

lowlights.title: Worst close-game luck in baseball
lowlights.body: A W vs Run Diff of -12.6 ranked last in the league and was the difference between a division title and a losing record. This kind of gap mostly evens out from year to year. Even so, a bullpen whose setup men walked hitters freely may have made some of it worse.

lowlights.title: The 6-22 May
lowlights.body: The Tigers were outscored 129-81 over the month, and it sank the season on its own. Outside May the team played above .500 with a large positive margin, so the month was a collapse, not a preview of the rest of the year.

lowlights.title: Soft lineup depth and poor defense
lowlights.body: The hitters graded D+ because heavy playing time went to McKinstry and Vierling, who were both well below average at the plate. The team defense cost 21.1 runs, and Torkelson and Hao-Yu Lee gave back a combined 16.6 Def Runs.

arc.note: A .500 start fell apart in a 6-22 May. The team recovered to play contender-level baseball through June and July, then went 24-28 over the last two months with a positive run margin it couldn't turn into wins.

recap.nextYear: The carryover is better than the record. A top-eight run differential, a staff ranked sixth in ERA and three hitters at All-Star level (McGonigle, Dingler, Greene) are the foundation, and the -12.6 W vs Run Diff is the part most likely to swing back. The cautions are in the peripherals. Melton's 2.76 ERA against a 4.09 FIP, and bullpen ERAs well under their FIPs (Waguespack 2.49 vs 4.55, Kinley 3.45 vs 5.21), mean the run prevention was partly flattering. The C+ rotation and C bullpen need real strikeout and walk improvement to keep it. The clearest areas to fix are the bottom of the lineup, the corner outfield in particular, and a defense that fell from +12.4 Fielding Runs in 2024 to -21.1.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; luck reading rests on a large, league-worst W vs Run Diff.
